root_cause: Escape key in a submenu incorrectly closes all submenus instead of only the current submenu because the handler calls this.elements.rootMenu.closeChildren().
repair_strategy: Replace the Escape handler in the non-top-level menu's _handleKeyup to close only the current submenu via its parent menu's toggle and move focus to that toggle, preserving parent submenu state.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will close only the innermost open submenu and return focus to its parent menubar item, keeping any parent submenus open as required.
functional_risks: If parentMenu is null (unlikely), the fallback behaves as before, closing all submenus.
If currentMenuItem.elements.toggle is missing, toggle.close() could throw; however this condition only occurs for legitimate submenu items.
Multiple nested submenus: Escape will close only the current submenu, which is correct behavior.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape while focus is on History (inside Facts submenu) results in focus on #facts, #facts aria-expanded false, and #about aria-expanded true.
Verify that Escape while focus is on Overview (inside About submenu) returns focus to #about and closes Overview.
Verify that Escape while focus is on #about (menubar item with submenu open) closes About submenu and returns focus to the menubar.
Verify that Escape when no submenu is open does not produce unexpected focus changes.
Ensure other keyboard navigation (ArrowRight, ArrowDown, etc.) continues to work as specified.
